chapter: Arrangers, Bill Robinson and Coleman Hawkins
title: Coleman Hawkins' styles and Benny Carter's influence
summary: Thomas argues Benny Carter influenced Hawkins' melodic turn and describes Hawkins as the man who made tenor saxophone respectable.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: And another thing I got on my mind (but my friend don't agree with me), I definitely think that Benny Carter had a great influence on Coleman Hawkins. Now, Coleman Hawkins may not admit it. Benny Carter sure won't admit it; he's such a great musician, he'll just brag about what a great musician Coleman... And he was great! But Coleman Hawkins was not playing melodic until he... They played together with...
Yeah. But see, they played together. And Benny Carter was always a melodic player.
I think they played with that band out of Detroit.

McKinney's Cotton Pickers or either Fletcher Henderson, one or the other. They played somewhere together. And Coleman Hawkins... See, Coleman Hawkins changed his style about three times. Because, you see, I idolized him as a saxophone player. Because when he was playing with Fletcher Henderson he was the rompiest, stompiest saxophone player I ever saw. He could break up a house just rompin' and stompin'. Yeah, and he stomped his foot around any (?) he was playing all at the same time.

Now, remember, Coleman hawkins was the first guy that played tenor saxophone. The tenor saxophone was a bastard instrument! -- until he picked it up. Nobody wanted it. I don't think there was... I'll have to check this back in the archives somewhere. I don't think there was even a tenor in the band until Coleman played tenor. And when he come out with this tenor saxophone, it was something... It was a new deal!

And he changed his style at least three times that I know of, and he changed it after he played with Benny Carter. Now, Benny Carter don't admit it. He admitted to playing with him, was all he could say when I got with him

one night to check it with him. It was all right ...(? )... But see, Benny Carter is such a gentleman, all he could say is how great Coleman... I know how great Coleman Hawkins was. But he was great... Because I can tell you all the great things he made with Fletcher Henderson after that. That's how I noticed it. Because Coleman Hawkins started to playing legato.
